note:
FEATURE / FAR-WORLD VISIBILITY ARCHITECTURE: Implement the code-grounded far-world visibility plan in this SceneIssue so terrain, semantic structures, settlements, forests, landmark natural features, and ordinary scatter remain visually coherent from the resident voxel world through the configured far horizon without making distant voxel regions resident. Preserve one deterministic world truth and choose representation by semantic importance, projected significance, readiness, and configured budgets rather than by scene-specific hard-coded distance behavior.

CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION BASELINE: `VoxelShowcase` keeps the near destructible voxel world resident to roughly 409.6 m and hands the outer view to `VoxelFarTerrain`. Far terrain is an analytic geometric clipmap. `FarFieldStructureStore` currently captures authored raised/lowered voxel surfaces and is point-sampled by far-terrain vertices; therefore known houses/castles are not represented independently and can be absent or malformed at sparse outer clipmap spacing. WorldBuilder already produces renderer-neutral semantic structure facts before physical voxel realization. Vegetation already has deterministic placement and persistent tree state plus procedural renderers. Extend those canonical systems; do not create parallel world ownership.

REQUIRED ARCHITECTURE: Keep broad terrain in `VoxelFarTerrain`; correct its guaranteed-coverage math and startup-fallback retirement. Produce renderer-neutral far-presentation descriptors from existing `StructureIntent`/`StructureForm`/`StructureSiteGeometry` planning output before voxel residency. Add a deterministic spatial visibility manifest, an engine-facing far-structure rendering contract, cached/instanced structure proxy HLOD, projected-size/semantic tier policy with hysteresis, and readiness-aware proxy-to-near-voxel handoff. Narrow `FarFieldStructureStore` to authored terrain/surface deviation and anonymous/arbitrary voxel fallback rather than using far-terrain samples as the primary representation of known semantic buildings. Add deterministic settlement clustering for distant towns. Extend existing vegetation/tree ownership with spatial visibility queries, simplified tree tiers, forest/canopy HLOD, and deterministic natural-scatter handling; promote exceptional natural features to landmark treatment instead of retaining every object.

NO DISTANT SIMULATION REQUIREMENT: Distant visibility must not imply full voxel residency, collision, physics, interiors, NPC simulation, gameplay scripts, or per-object Unity GameObjects. Lightweight metadata/proxy/cluster representations are the intended far state. Persistent destruction/state changes must flow from existing authoritative structure/tree/world state into far presentation rather than introducing duplicate persistence.

REUSE BOUNDARIES: WorldBuilder remains renderer-neutral. VoxelEngine Rendering must not depend on Game/WorldBuilder types. Scene/game visibility thresholds and named-content policy belong in composition/configuration. Preserve the existing near `VoxelSurfaceScheduler` source-step/ring algorithm unless a separate demonstrated defect requires modification; only expose the minimum readiness information needed for representation handoff. Preserve existing vegetation/tree identity and damage state as authoritative.

TESTING ARCHITECTURE: Follow the repository's module-validation architecture. Focused behavioral tests belong to the owning modules. Player-visible proof must use the shared standalone-player harness through module-owned validation scenes/scenarios automatically discovered by CI, plus the canonical built-player `KentridgePlayableSlice` assembled-game integration gate. Do not use top-level VoxelShowcase/Kentridge-only screenshots as the sole validation for reusable rendering/WorldBuilder modules, and do not add feature-specific behavior to the generic capture harness.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) A declared landmark remains visible at 8 km, 10 km, and 12 km from cardinal and diagonal views, including representative/worst camera-snap phases, without requiring its voxel regions to be resident.
(2) A never-visited declared landmark can appear from deterministic macro-world/WorldBuilder metadata before physical voxel realization.
(3) Broad terrain, semantic structures, settlements, and deterministic natural scatter use independent appropriate distance representations while sharing one deterministic world definition and no duplicate authority.
(4) Forested mountains remain visibly forested at horizon distance without retaining or drawing every individual tree; ordinary sub-pixel vegetation/rocks naturally cull while exceptional natural landmarks retain appropriate proxies.
(5) Near/proxy/cluster representation transitions use readiness plus hysteresis/overlap so approach and retreat do not create a missing-object frame, unstable tier oscillation, or prolonged double representation.
(6) The configured far radius is geometrically guaranteed by testable clipmap coverage math; startup fallback is not retired until authoritative coverage is actually complete.
(7) Known semantic houses/castles no longer depend on a sparse far-terrain vertex landing inside their footprint. `FarFieldStructureStore` continues to support terrain deviations and anonymous/arbitrary voxel fallback without double-rendering semantic structures.
(8) Dense settlements use deterministic cluster HLOD at far range while preserving major anchors/landmark silhouettes and bounded draw/instance counts.
(9) Far structure rendering uses cached/batched/instanced proxy data rather than one persistent Unity GameObject or resident voxel region per distant building.
(10) Existing deterministic vegetation placement and `TreeWorldState` remain authoritative; far tiers/query indexes do not create a second tree/plant persistence model. Persistent sever/destroy state is reflected in distant presentation.
(11) Shared APIs remain semantic/config-driven and renderer-neutral at their ownership boundaries; scene-specific thresholds and named-content decisions remain in composition/configuration.
(12) Focused regressions prove deterministic records/query order, never-resident visibility, coverage guarantees, HLOD stability, no duplicate semantic/fallback representation, and persistent-state propagation through production computation.
(13) Built-player module validation directly demonstrates structure HLOD, settlement clustering, vegetation/canopy HLOD, and transition behavior through their owning module validation scenes/scenarios; visual acceptance does not rely on PlayMode-rendered screenshots.
(14) The canonical built-player `KentridgePlayableSlice` integration gate demonstrates the systems composing in the actual game without startup/runtime exceptions, missing far terrain, visible representation holes, or incompatible WorldBuilder/rendering integration.
(15) CPU, GPU, draw/instance count, memory, generation/query cost, and transition churn are measured against repository/device budgets. Do not increase near voxel residency or weaken unrelated budgets/tolerances to satisfy far visibility.
(16) Complete every required checkbox in `tasks.md`; if the same acceptance symptom/assertion survives two materially different fixes, isolate a minimal repro/root cause before another speculative change.

The detailed selected design is in `architecture-proposal.md`; implementation sequencing and gates are in `plan.md`; the exact code-grounded checklist is in `tasks.md`.
